title: MAHADEVI KANYA PATHSHALA SOCIETY versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 2265 of 2025 (M/S)
Mahadevi Kanya Pathshala Society and Another ........Petitioners

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others ........Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. S.N. Babulkar, Advocate General with Mr. C.S. Rawat, Chief Standing
Counsle and Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, A.G.A. for the State/respondent nos.
1 and 2.
Mr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, Advocate for the respondent no.3.
Mr. Shashank Pandey (through video conferencing) and Mr. Akshay
Pradhan, Advocates for the Caveator.
Mr. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate for the Caveator (Principal).
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Heard.
2. Admit.
3. Learned C.S.C. takes notices for the respondent nos. 1
and 2.
4. Mr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, Advocate takes notices for the
respondent no. 3.
5. Respondents may file counter affidavit within four weeks.
6. Two weeks, thereafter, rejoinder affidavit, if any, may be
filed.
7. List thereafter for final hearing.
8. Heard on Stay Application, IA No1 of 2025.
9. The challenge in this petition is made to the public notice
dated 26.07.2025, issued under Section 57 of the U.P. State
Universities Act, 1973 ("the Act").
10. The petitioners-society runs Mahadevi Kanya Pathshala
(PG) College, Dehradun ("the college"). According to the impugned
notice, the society of the college is not registered. Therefore, there is no
system to run the college; the employees are not being paid salary;
teaching and non-teaching staff is not being appointed or promoted;
the service related issues of the personnel are not being decided,

2
which, in turn, is affecting the academic activities of the college and as
a result, the number of students is decreasing year by year. Keeping in
view all those factors, the impugned notice records that an Authorised
Controller is proposed to be appointed under Section 58 of the Act.
Therefore, objections have been invited that if any person has any
objections to the appointment of Authorised Controller, he may file
response till 04.08.2025. By means of the stay application, the
petitioners seek stay of the effect and operation of the impugned
notice.
11. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the
society has a Management Committee, which is still working; merely
because the registration of the society is not renewed, it does not
become defunct until it is dissolved under Section 13-A of the Societies
Registration Act, 1860. He refers to the principles of law, as laid down
by the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in the case of Girja Singh Vs.
Committee of Management Intermediate College, Amethi, 2022 SCC
OnLine All 1083, wherein, the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court has, inter
alia, observed that, "a society once registered, will not get extinct,
that is to say, it will not become non-existent in absence of
renewal of the certificate of registration after expiry of the term
of registration.........................................................................The
society will get extinct only when it is dissolved as per the
provisions contained in section 13 or 13-A of the Act."
12. He also submits that the notice is bad in the eye of law
because it records that no Management Committee of the society is
functional; there are regular elections of the Management Committee
and at present also, the Management Committee is functional; notice
under Section 57 of the Act is to be given to the Management
Committee alone; it cannot be given to public at large; beyond
statutory provisions, notice may not be given; the impugned notice is
merely an eye wash; the respondents-authority have pre-decided the

3
issue to appoint an Authorised Controller. He would refer to the
contents of the notice, wherein, it is stated that Authorised Controller
is to be appointed for the college; in case the impugned notice is
allowed to remain in operation, the petitioners may be permitted to
raise all the issues in response to the notice and they may be given an
opportunity of personal hearing as well; if any person other than the
Management Committee files response to the notice, a copy of it may
be provided to the petitioners also so that they can effectively make
their representation before the authorities concerned.
13. Learned C.S.C. submits that the college is not
functioning; the Management Committee is not in existence; the
society has not renewed its registration; teaching and non-teaching
staff is not being paid salary; there has been no appointment in the
recent past; the educational activities have gone down and the number
of students have also decreased.
14. Learned Advocate General submits that the provisions of
Section 57 of the Act are emergent provisions; they are not easily
invoked, but the functioning of the college is such that it has become
necessary to invoke this provision.
15. There have been multiple litigations between the
Management Committee and the State with regard to functioning of
the college. In fact, earlier, in Writ Petition (M/S) Mo.853 of 2015,
Mahadevi Kanya Pathshala College Society Vs. Commissioner Garhwal
Mandal, Pauri Garhwal and others, and connected matter ("the first
petition") was decided by this Court on 08.01.2020, when the Court
had directed the Deputy Registrar to convene a meeting of all the
members of the Society for election of the Managing Committee within
three months since then, but it is admitted that this order dated
08.01.2020 of the first petition has been stayed by the Hon'ble
Supreme Court and the appeal is still pending.

4
16. Learned counsel for the petitioners has also submitted
that in the past, on multiple occasions, the State Government had
appointed Authorised Controller, intruding into the functioning of the
Management Committee, which has hampered the working of the
college.
17. Today, in the morning session, when the matter was
taken up, this Court requested learned counsel for the petitioners to
give a statement on the followings:-
"1) What is the total strength of the teaching and non-teaching
staff and what is the working strength today?
2) Has salary been paid regularly to the teaching and non-teaching staff of the College? And; if not, what is the status?
When for the last time salary was paid to the teaching and
non-teaching staff?
3) When for the last time, recruitments were made in the
teaching staff and when for the last time recruitments were
made to the non-teaching staff?
4) If the above are not regular, who is responsible to it? And
lastly;
5) As to what is the strength of students in the last three years?"
18. In response to it, learned counsel for the petitioners has
submitted a written text. Let it be taken on record.
19. According to it, there are 62 sanctioned posts of teaching
staff in the college, out of which only 14, including the Principal, are
working. It also reveals that no teachers were appointed after January,
2012.
20. In respect of non-teaching staff, it is revealed that the
total sanctioned strength is 69, out of which 31 are functional and last
regular appointment in the non-teaching staff was made in the year
2001, and one person was appointed on compassionate ground in the
year 2023. The sanctioned strength of the students is 3,000, but since
2020-2021, it has decreased in the following order:-
Serial No. Academic Year Strength of
the students.
(i) 2020-2021 3442
(ii) 2021-2022 3348

5
(iii) 2022-2023 3252
(iv) 2023-2024 2498
(v) 2024-2025 2075
21. The report also reveals that since March, 2025, salary
was not paid to the teaching and non-teaching staff. What is revealed
by the petitioners, per se, reveals that all is not well in the college.
22. Learned counsel for the petitioners has read over the
provisions of Section 57 of the Act to argue that, in fact, it is not
attracted in the instant case.
23. This Court refrains to make deeper scrutiny of those
aspects at this stage. Fact remains that teaching and non-teaching
staff has not been appointed in the college for long despite numerous
vacancies. There have been consistently lower strength of the
students, which were admitted in the preceding years. Salaries have
not been paid.
24. Section 57 of the Act requires the State Government to
call upon the Management to show cause why an order under Section
58 of the Act should not be made. This is what is written in the
impugned notice. It records that action under Section 58 of the Act is
to be taken. In strict sense, it may not be said to be prejudging or pre-deciding the issue that in all probability, Authorised Controller is to be
appointed. By the impugned notice, response from public at large has
been invited.
25. The petitioners claim that the Management Committee is
in existence, whereas, State does not recognize it.
26. Learned Advocate General submits that if notices are
given to other members of the society, it does not make the impugned
notice bad in the eyes of law; the members of the Management
Committee have been given individual notices.
27. Learned C.S.C. submits that, in fact, individual notices
have been given to the petitioner no.2 also.

6
28. Be it as it may, having considered the functional position
of the college and other attending factors, this Court is of the view that
at this stage, the operation of the impugned notice may not be stayed.
Accordingly, the stay application deserves to be rejected.
29. The stay application is rejected.
30. However, the respondents shall supply a copy of the
response, which are received pursuant to the impugned notice. The
respondents shall also provide an opportunity of personal hearing to
the petitioners. Needless to say, the respondents-authority shall
consider the response that may be filed by the petitioners or any other
person and decide the matter strictly in accordance with the provisions
as contained under Sections 57, 58 of the Act or under any other
enabling provisions of law, by a reasoned and speaking order.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J) 31.07.2025
Ravi Bisht
